Scope: Supported user-script facade and helpers in HL7Workbench.Scripting, API 2. Inherited .NET members and compiler-generated record equality, printing, copying and deconstruction use ordinary C# semantics; they are not host operations. Host transport/orchestration types are classified separately and are not supported authoring facilities.

InfrastructureTypes.ScriptDefinition: Host submission and API-version DTO, not a script entry point.
InfrastructureTypes.ScriptWorkerOptions: Parent process configuration; scripts cannot reconfigure their owning worker.
InfrastructureTypes.ScriptWorkerSession: Parent worker orchestration/transport, not a facade operation.

Entries.Title: Main / Complete and execution scopes
Entries.Description: Initialization runs once, Main once per captured selected message in logical input order, then optional Complete once after all Main calls succeed. Top-level variables persist within a run; each Run starts a fresh worker. Select Current message or Whole document in the editor. The host performs iteration; there is no document enumeration/navigation API in scripts.
Entries.Parameters: Main/Complete: no parameters. Scope is selected by the application, not changed from inside Main.
Entries.Returns: Both entry points return void. A successful run publishes a new independent unsaved output document.
Entries.Limitations: Exactly one top-level instance, synchronous, nongeneric, parameterless void Main and at most one matching Complete. No overloads, static/async/Task entries or background work. Failure skips Complete and discards staged output/reports. Never retain Message or ScriptSegment across invocations.
Entries.Keywords: lifecycle initialization scope batch loop iterate messages

Entries.Title: Built-ins, My Scripts and starter examples
Entries.Signature: Duplicate Script → Rename Script → Save Script
Entries.Description: Built-in scripts are application-owned read-only entries. Duplicate Script saves an independent copy in My Scripts with a new ID. Rename and edit that copy, Save Script, reopen it and Run. Built-in updates do not rewrite user copies. Starter topics offer Create editable script, which creates an unsaved draft through the normal unsaved-change prompt.
Entries.Parameters: Use a descriptive local name (1–120 characters, no control characters). Choose Apply to scope before Run.
Entries.Returns: Saved user records keep their own stable identity and source. Ctrl+S in the script editor saves the script.
Entries.Limitations: Saving a script does not save HL7 output. Dirty drafts prompt before switching; failed saves keep the draft. Old development scripts require explicit rewrite/adoption. Duplicate Patient Deidentifier to configure its supported policy rather than creating another library preset.
Entries.Keywords: library built-in immutable duplicate rename save reopen templates starter user scripts

Entries.Title: ScriptGlobals: Message, Batch, Cancellation
Entries.Description: The worker supplies these globals without construction. Message resolves to the current Main invocation; Batch owns this job’s advanced facilities; Cancellation is the run token.
Entries.Parameters: No parameters. Use Cancellation.ThrowIfCancellationRequested() inside long loops.
Entries.Returns: Message is the bounded current facade, Batch the same run object and Cancellation the same execution token.
Entries.Limitations: Message is unavailable during initialization and Complete (LifecyclePhase). Do not cache a facade, start background callbacks, or suppress cancellation.

Entries.Title: ScriptMessage.Read: inspect value state
Entries.Description: Reads the original encoded spelling and its structural state without implicitly decoding HL7 escapes. Prefer this before Text when a field may be absent or explicitly null.
Entries.Parameters: path: Core path such as PID-5.1, PID[2]-3[2].4.1, or OBX-5.1.2. Omitted segment/repetition indexes mean 1.
Entries.Returns: ScriptValue with State and nullable Raw; no value is silently substituted for missing/null.
Entries.Limitations: Coordinates are one-based, not byte/editor offsets. Missing, empty and explicit null stay distinct. No arbitrary segment insertion or delimiter/header replacement is exposed. Core validates writes and preserves unrelated bytes, encoding, separators and terminators.
Entries.Keywords: read field component subcomponent path missing explicit null raw

Entries.Title: ScriptMessage.Text: decoded text
Entries.Description: Explicitly decodes HL7 escape sequences using the message’s delimiters. An existing empty value returns an empty string.
Entries.Parameters: path: one-based Core HL7 coordinates, independent of actual separator characters.
Entries.Returns: Decoded string; throws a fixed MissingValue diagnostic for missing/null or DecodeDiagnostic for unresolved escapes.
Entries.Limitations: Coordinates are one-based, not byte/editor offsets. Missing, empty and explicit null stay distinct. No arbitrary segment insertion or delimiter/header replacement is exposed. Core validates writes and preserves unrelated bytes, encoding, separators and terminators.

Entries.Title: ScriptValue and ValueState
Entries.Signature:
record ScriptValue(ValueState State, string? Raw)
enum ValueState { Missing, Empty, ExplicitNull, Value }
Entries.Description: State distinguishes no structural position, an existing empty position, HL7 explicit null (two quotes), and a nonempty value. Raw preserves escape spelling rather than decoded text.
Entries.Parameters: State: structural state. Raw: original spelling supplied by Read; null for missing positions.
Entries.Returns: Read returns a value record; constructing one does not modify a message.
Entries.Limitations: Record equality/with/deconstruction are ordinary generated C# features. Only controlled ScriptMessage/ScriptSegment methods mutate HL7.

Entries.Title: ScriptMessage.SetText: write a literal
Entries.Description: Writes a literal value through Core, escaping reserved characters for the actual message delimiters. Use for generated names and other literal replacements.
Entries.Parameters: path: supported existing or expandable field coordinate. value: literal text, not pre-escaped HL7.
Entries.Returns: No return value; invalid paths/unsafe edits fail with fixed diagnostics.
Entries.Limitations: Coordinates are one-based, not byte/editor offsets. Missing, empty and explicit null stay distinct. No arbitrary segment insertion or delimiter/header replacement is exposed. Core validates writes and preserves unrelated bytes, encoding, separators and terminators.
Entries.Keywords: write field literal escaped SetText independent output

Entries.Title: ScriptMessage.SetRaw: explicit HL7 spelling
Entries.Description: Writes explicitly encoded HL7 spelling through Core validation. Prefer SetText for literal data so custom delimiters and escape characters are encoded correctly.
Entries.Parameters: path: supported Core coordinate. value: raw HL7 spelling in the message’s delimiters.
Entries.Returns: No return value; rejection retains the previous model.
Entries.Limitations: Coordinates are one-based, not byte/editor offsets. Missing, empty and explicit null stay distinct. No arbitrary segment insertion or delimiter/header replacement is exposed. Core validates writes and preserves unrelated bytes, encoding, separators and terminators.

Entries.Title: ScriptMessage.SetNull and Clear
Entries.Signature:
void SetNull(string path)
void Clear(string path)
Entries.Description: SetNull writes an explicit HL7 null. Clear empties an existing position without removing it; a missing target is a no-op.
Entries.Parameters: path: Core one-based coordinate.
Entries.Returns: No return value. Missing, empty and explicit null have different meanings.
Entries.Limitations: Coordinates are one-based, not byte/editor offsets. Missing, empty and explicit null stay distinct. No arbitrary segment insertion or delimiter/header replacement is exposed. Core validates writes and preserves unrelated bytes, encoding, separators and terminators.

Entries.Title: ScriptMessage.CanEdit / HasDiagnostics
Entries.Signature:
bool CanEdit { get; }
bool HasDiagnostics { get; }
Entries.Description: CanEdit exposes Core editability. HasDiagnostics reports any structural/encoding diagnostic, allowing conservative scripts to refuse malformed input before writing.
Entries.Parameters: No parameters.
Entries.Returns: Booleans, not a conformance or privacy guarantee.
Entries.Limitations: Do not silently normalize malformed input. A script may explicitly throw to fail the run or leave the message unchanged for review.

Entries.Title: Segments and repeated fields
Entries.Description: Enumerates address views for a three-character segment identifier, in occurrence order. Each view re-resolves against the current model after writes; Identifier and one-based Occurrence identify the segment.
Entries.Parameters: identifier: segment ID, for example PID or OBX, without field/path suffixes.
Entries.Returns: Read-only list (empty if no match). Repetition indexes remain explicit in relative paths.
Entries.Limitations: Coordinates are one-based, not byte/editor offsets. Missing, empty and explicit null stay distinct. No arbitrary segment insertion or delimiter/header replacement is exposed. Core validates writes and preserves unrelated bytes, encoding, separators and terminators.
Entries.Keywords: Segments ScriptSegment occurrence repetition repeat custom delimiters

Entries.Parameters: relativePath: field/repetition/component/subcomponent without segment prefix, for example 5[2].1. value (when present): literal for SetText, encoded spelling for SetRaw.
Entries.Returns: ScriptValue with State and Raw.
Entries.Limitations: Coordinates are one-based, not byte/editor offsets. Missing, empty and explicit null stay distinct. No arbitrary segment insertion or delimiter/header replacement is exposed. Core validates writes and preserves unrelated bytes, encoding, separators and terminators.

Entries.Title: HL7 paths, repetitions and custom delimiters
Entries.Description: The first example addresses segment occurrence 2, field 3, repetition 2, component 4, subcomponent 1. Addresses use Core coordinates, not literal separators. The parser reads MSH delimiters, so no script should split raw composites on ^, ~ or &.
Entries.Parameters: Indexes are positive and one-based. Segment-only reads and special MSH positions follow Core path/edit rules.
Entries.Returns: Read/Text/controlled mutations use the same coordinate grammar.
Entries.Limitations: Coordinates are one-based, not byte/editor offsets. Missing, empty and explicit null stay distinct. No arbitrary segment insertion or delimiter/header replacement is exposed. Core validates writes and preserves unrelated bytes, encoding, separators and terminators.
Entries.Keywords: path syntax repeated fields custom delimiters component subcomponent MSH encoding

Entries.Title: ScriptMessage.Exclude
Entries.Description: Omits the current message’s normal output. It does not cancel the job or suppress an already held/deferred copy.
Entries.Parameters: No parameters. Call during Main.
Entries.Returns: No return value.
Entries.Limitations: Filtering/deferred output requires extractable plain messages or complete unambiguous MLLP envelopes. Batch wrappers/opaque regions cannot be silently discarded; unsafe boundaries fail atomically.

Entries.Title: ScriptBatch.MessageNumber
Entries.Description: One-based job-local input ordinal during Main; zero in initialization and Complete. With Current scope it is 1 even when the selected source message has a different document position.
Entries.Parameters: No parameters.
Entries.Returns: Job ordinal, not a stable MessageId, document position, output counter or navigation command.
Entries.Limitations: Source mapping stays in the parent. Tab switches do not retarget a captured run. Never persist job ordinals as document identity.

Entries.Title: ScriptBatch.SetOutputFileName
Entries.Description: Suggests an output filename in initialization, Main or Complete. The last valid suggestion wins. Invalid suggestions are ignored with a fixed nonfatal notice; they never erase a valid suggestion.
Entries.Parameters: fileName: filename only, up to 128 UTF-16 units including .hl7; the extension is appended/standardized. Paths, reserved Windows devices, controls, format characters and unsafe endings are refused.
Entries.Returns: No return value. Without an override, the captured script name or Script Result.hl7 is used.
Entries.Limitations: A filename suggestion never saves, chooses a directory or authorizes replacement. Duplicate tab labels may gain a display counter without changing the suggestion.
Entries.Keywords: SetOutputFileName filename naming Save As output

Entries.Title: ScriptOutputFileName validation
Entries.Description: The same portable Windows filename policy is available to scripts. FromScriptName uses Fallback if normalization fails; TryNormalize returns a success flag and an empty out string on failure.
Entries.Parameters: name/suggestion: proposed filename, never a path. fileName: normalized output when true.
Entries.Returns: FromScriptName returns a safe suggestion. TryNormalize returns bool and normalized text.
Entries.Limitations: No filesystem lookup, truncation, normalization of Unicode or extraction from paths. Other suffixes become part of the stem before .hl7 is appended.

Entries.Title: ScriptBatch.Hold and ScriptDeferredMessage
Entries.Signature:
ScriptDeferredMessage Hold(ScriptMessage message)
sealed class ScriptDeferredMessage // opaque; no public constructor or members
Entries.Description: Retains an immutable bounded copy of the current transformed message for a later decision. Normal output remains included unless Exclude is called separately.
Entries.Parameters: message: exactly the current Message during Main.
Entries.Returns: Opaque copy owned by this run; no raw byte or mapping-table access.
Entries.Limitations: Hold is unavailable outside Main. Up to 128 retained copies / 16 MiB per job. Copies retain original input attribution and framing constraints.

Entries.Title: ScriptBatch.Defer
Entries.Description: Holds and queues a copy immediately during Main. Queued copies drain after Complete in queue order, after normal output.
Entries.Parameters: message: exactly the current Message during Main.
Entries.Returns: No return value.
Entries.Limitations: Retained and queued copies have separate 128-message/16 MiB shared job budgets. Defer does not exclude normal output by itself. No source-free message generation.

Entries.Title: ScriptBatch.Emit
Entries.Description: Queues one of this run’s held copies during Complete. Emission follows normal output and already deferred copies, in Emit call order.
Entries.Parameters: copy: immutable handle returned by this run’s Hold.
Entries.Returns: No return value.
Entries.Limitations: Only Complete and same-owner handles are accepted. Repeated emission consumes the queue budget again. Failure or cancellation publishes neither partial output nor reports.

Entries.Title: Atomic output, attribution and source edits
Entries.Signature: Main → Complete → deferred drain → validated independent output
Entries.Description: Workspace captures stable input identity/revision, stages all transformed messages and CSV privately, validates output framing and publishes only after success. Original source bytes, drafts, undo history and save destination are untouched.
Entries.Parameters: Choose Current or Whole in the editor; output always opens as a new unsaved document.
Entries.Returns: A successful result keeps producing-run attribution. Source edits during execution preserve independent captured output with explicit stale-source attribution.
Entries.Limitations: Closing the source, cancellation or failures prevent publication. Invalid input/output, unsafe extraction or framing changes fail explicitly. Reports require explicit export. Arbitrary external C# side effects cannot be rolled back.
Entries.Keywords: atomic publication stale source independent snapshot output generation

Entries.Title: ScriptBatch.Report / ScriptCsvReport.Row
Entries.Signature:
ScriptCsvReport Report(string name, params string[] columns)
void ScriptCsvReport.Row(params string?[] values)
Entries.Description: Define ordered report schemas only during initialization. Append rows during initialization, Main or Complete. Reports are staged with output and become exportable only after a successful run.
Entries.Parameters: name: 1–64 ASCII letters/digits/_/-, case-insensitively unique. columns: 1–64 headings in order. values: same count/order; null and empty both export as empty quoted cells.
Entries.Returns: Report returns a run-owned CSV writer. Row returns void.
Entries.Limitations: 8 reports; 100,000 data rows/16 MiB UTF-8 globally; 16,384 UTF-16 units/cell; 256 KiB per lifecycle operation. UTF-8 no BOM, CRLF, all cells quoted. Formula-like cells gain an apostrophe. Keep reports bounded and avoid sensitive content.
Entries.Keywords: Report CSV ScriptCsvReport Row bounded count

Entries.Title: ScriptBatch.ValidReportName
Entries.Description: Checks the bounded ASCII report-label grammar without accessing a filesystem.
Entries.Parameters: name: non-null candidate label, 1–64 ASCII letters/digits, underscore or hyphen.
Entries.Returns: True for a valid label; uniqueness is checked by Report.
Entries.Example:
var valid = ScriptBatch.ValidReportName("summary");
void Main() {}
Entries.Limitations: A report label is not a file path. Invalid Report schemas fail ReportSchema; byte/row/cell exhaustion fails ReportLimit.

Entries.Title: ScriptDiagnostic and ScriptPhase
Entries.Description: Diagnostics describe safe codes/locations, not imported exception messages. The editor presents compiler locations and captured input attribution. Description maps codes to fixed text; ToString formats that safe metadata.
Entries.Parameters: Phase: failing operation. Code: fixed/CS compiler code. Line/Column: one-based script location. MessageNumber: job-local ordinal. Path: validated HL7 coordinate when available.
Entries.Returns: Read-only metadata and formatted description. Constructing metadata does not publish it automatically.
Entries.Limitations: Worker sanitization accepts a closed code/path set and omits arbitrary source text and exception messages. Never put identifiers or patient values in diagnostics; unknown text is not a safe logging channel. Compiler codes take precedence before initialization.
Entries.Keywords: ScriptDiagnostic ScriptPhase Description ToString errors compile runtime

Entries.Title: ScriptRunException.Diagnostics
Entries.Signature:
ScriptRunException(params ScriptDiagnostic[] diagnostics)
IReadOnlyList<ScriptDiagnostic> Diagnostics { get; }
Entries.Description: Signals a fixed scripting failure to the worker. Prefer allowing transformation and resource-limit failures to abort the run.
Entries.Parameters: diagnostics: fixed safe diagnostic records, without source values.
Entries.Returns: Exception carries the diagnostic list; inherited Exception members are ordinary .NET members.
Entries.Limitations: Do not catch errors merely to publish partial data; cancellation/limits should propagate. Imported exception text is omitted by the worker.

Entries.Title: ScriptLimits: fixed worker facade budgets
Entries.Description: These public constants bound script source UTF-16 units, complete-message UTF-16 units, segment units, encoded message bytes, diagnostics, inputs, deferred copies and CSV operations. They are not user-settable options.
Entries.Parameters: No parameters. Character limits use UTF-16; byte limits count encoded payload or UTF-8 CSV, as named.
Entries.Returns: Compile-time integer constants.
Entries.Limitations: Defaults outside this facade: 768 MiB worker memory, 30s startup, 60s compilation, 10s each operation, 10min job, 1 GiB input/output storage, 12 MiB IPC frame. Host configuration may impose tighter bounds. Long loops must check Cancellation; timeout forcibly stops an uncooperative worker.
Entries.Keywords: ScriptLimits timeout memory bytes characters cancellation limits

Entries.Title: Trusted C#, isolation and cancellation
Entries.Description: Scripts run in a fresh local ScriptHost process with bounded transport, journals, deadlines and Windows job memory containment. This is trusted C# running with the user’s permissions, not an operating-system security sandbox. Only run code you trust.
Entries.Parameters: The cancellation token is available in every phase. Use it in long loops and helper calls.
Entries.Returns: Canceled/failed runs publish no partial output or reports; safe diagnostics omit imported exception text.
Entries.Limitations: #r, #load and #line directives are refused. This does not prevent arbitrary trusted C# filesystem/network side effects; those cannot be rolled back. The documented synthetic helpers themselves have no IO/network or persistent mappings. No new execution capability is added by the reference. No async/background facade use.
Entries.Keywords: security offline isolation sandbox permissions directives cancellation network filesystem

Entries.Title: SyntheticIdentityLibrary construction and Get
Entries.Description: Allocates deterministic fictional profiles from the bundled vocabulary, with bounded collision probing. Construct once in initialization for within-run identity consistency. Already public and usable in authored scripts; no extra facade is required.
Entries.Parameters: seed: reproducibility configuration, not an anonymity secret. maximumIdentities: 1–100,000. identityKey: nonempty opaque key, at most 256 UTF-16 units. cancellation: execution token.
Entries.Returns: Same library/key returns the cached complete profile; distinct allocations do not reuse complete identities. No mapping tables are exposed.
Entries.Limitations: Determinism requires the same seed, key/allocation order, dictionary and implementation. New runs require new instances; no key/profile map is persisted. Exhaustion uses TransformationLimit. Names and finite fictional phone numbers can repeat. Do not use source demographics to select replacements. Review required: these are test-data aids, not a guarantee of PHI removal or compliance. Container bytes, nested metadata and retained clinical values require separate review. Do not log keys, profiles or source values.
Entries.Keywords: SyntheticIdentityLibrary Get DictionaryVersion deterministic seed identity profiles

Entries.Title: SyntheticIdentity profile and construction
Entries.Signature: record SyntheticIdentity(int Allocation, string GivenName, string MiddleName, string FamilyName, string Street, string Locality, DateOnly DateOfBirth, string AdministrativeSex, string MaritalStatus)
Entries.Description: Library-generated profiles contain allocation slot, invented given/middle/family names, fictional street/locality, a fixed-pool DOB, administrative sex and marital status. Source demographics and the clock do not choose these values.
Entries.Parameters: Allocation: library slot. GivenName/MiddleName/FamilyName: vocabulary names. Street/Locality: fictional address. DateOfBirth: generated date. AdministrativeSex/MaritalStatus: generated codes.
Entries.Returns: A value record; prefer library.Get rather than manually constructing an inconsistent profile.
Entries.Limitations: Positional properties support record init/with syntax but do not validate manually created records. DOB pool spans 1945–2013; profiles are test values, not clinical conformance or real-world identities. Review required: these are test-data aids, not a guarantee of PHI removal or compliance. Container bytes, nested metadata and retained clinical values require separate review. Do not log keys, profiles or source values.

Entries.Title: DeidentificationWorkflow construction and Apply
Entries.Description: Construct once in initialization; Apply the current Message in Main. Summary returns fixed count-only metadata, and ShiftDays exposes the common calendar-day offset for this run. Patient policy uses qualified identities and conservative field handling. Findings returns up to 1,000 structural review occurrences with fixed reasons, never original values.
Entries.Parameters: options: supported preset/seed/shift/mapping bounds. cancellation: run token. message: current invocation facade.
Entries.Returns: Apply returns void; Summary is a count snapshot suitable for one Complete report row. Existing library built-ins provide the complete reviewable presets.
Entries.Limitations: Do not instantiate per Main when cross-message consistency matters. Apply requires editable input without diagnostics. Patient unsupported/narrative/ED leaves are suppressed; narrower presets retain other sensitive values. Qualified identity ambiguity is counted, never guessed. Review required: these are test-data aids, not a guarantee of PHI removal or compliance. Container bytes, nested metadata and retained clinical values require separate review. Do not log keys, profiles or source values.
Entries.Keywords: DeidentificationWorkflow Apply Summary timestamp shifting consistent identity patient

Entries.Title: DeidentificationOptions and presets
Entries.Description: Immutable configuration for existing helpers. Patient Deidentifier replaces supported identity/demographics and suppresses unsupported leaves. Identifier Pseudonymizer changes supported references only; Timestamp Shifter changes supported timestamps only.
Entries.Parameters: Preset: one of three enum values. Seed: deterministic run seed. ShiftDays: -3660…3660, or null for a derived nonzero -365…365 displacement. MaximumMappings: 1–100,000 per map.
Entries.Returns: A configuration record validated by the workflow constructor.
Entries.Limitations: Full-day through second precision, up to four fraction digits and explicit offsets are preserved. Missing offsets stay absent. Partial/malformed/overflow/leap-second/unsupported timestamps are cleared in Patient or retained with counts in Timestamp mode. No timezone/locale guessing. Review required: these are test-data aids, not a guarantee of PHI removal or compliance. Container bytes, nested metadata and retained clinical values require separate review. Do not log keys, profiles or source values.
Entries.Keywords: DeidentificationOptions Preset Seed ShiftDays MaximumMappings timestamp date precision

Entries.Title: DeidentificationSummary counters
Entries.Signature: record DeidentificationSummary(long Messages, long MissingIdentities, long AmbiguousIdentities, long ReplacedValues, long SuppressedValues, long ShiftedTimestamps, long UnsupportedTimestamps, long UnknownSegments, long HighRiskFields, long RetainedValues)
Entries.Description: Messages: processed count. MissingIdentities/AmbiguousIdentities: unresolved correlation counts. ReplacedValues/SuppressedValues: transformed/suppressed leaves. ShiftedTimestamps/UnsupportedTimestamps: supported/unsupported time counts. UnknownSegments/HighRiskFields/RetainedValues: review evidence counts.
Entries.Parameters: Constructor parameters are the named long counters; workflows populate them. No source values are present.
Entries.Returns: Count snapshot, not a persisted source-to-profile map or an assertion of anonymity.
Entries.Limitations: Counts cover the supported policy only. Do not manufacture a successful privacy report from a manually constructed summary. Review required: these are test-data aids, not a guarantee of PHI removal or compliance. Container bytes, nested metadata and retained clinical values require separate review. Do not log keys, profiles or source values.
Entries.Keywords: DeidentificationSummary counts counters missing ambiguous timestamps

Entries.Title: Summary metadata, categories and CSV projection
Entries.Description: Counts and preset/category metadata from the producing execution. Status is Completed — review required when specific identity, timestamp, unknown-segment, high-risk or retained-review counts are nonzero; otherwise Completed — no flagged findings. ScopeNotice is a separate general limitation, never a detected finding.
Entries.Parameters: No method parameters. Define Batch.Report with Columns in initialization and call Row(Summary.Cells) once in Complete.
Entries.Returns: Read-only metadata and fresh arrays. A validated built-in report is associated with its output document’s Transformation Report panel.
Entries.Limitations: CSV keeps the original columns in order and appends Retained values requiring review and Omitted findings. The Status wording and unassessed-scope notice are updated. No source values, filenames or mappings. No flagged findings is not certification or permission to disclose. Existing script copies without a findings CSV show counts with details unavailable.
Entries.Keywords: Categories Columns Cells Status ScopeNotice Transformation Report export

Entries.Title: DeidentificationCategoryCount and categories
Entries.Signature:
record DeidentificationCategoryCount(DeidentificationCategory Category, long Transformed, long Suppressed)
enum DeidentificationCategory { Names, Addresses, Contacts, Demographics, Identifiers, Providers, Narratives, Attachments, Other }
Entries.Description: Groups supported leaf operations into names, addresses, contacts, demographics, identifiers, providers, narratives, attachments and other fields.
Entries.Parameters: Category: fixed category. Transformed: replacement count. Suppressed: cleared-leaf count.
Entries.Returns: Count record in Summary.Categories; no raw content or mapping keys.
Entries.Limitations: A category count is scope evidence, not proof that all sensitive content in that category was found. Review required: these are test-data aids, not a guarantee of PHI removal or compliance. Container bytes, nested metadata and retained clinical values require separate review. Do not log keys, profiles or source values.

Entries.Title: Structural de-identification findings
Entries.Description: Fixed structural coordinates and reasons for manual review. No original values are present. Unknown segment names are replaced by the fixed Unknown vocabulary entry.
Entries.Parameters: MessageNumber is the one-based processed ordinal within this workflow, not a current source position. SegmentNumber is the one-based absolute segment position; SegmentOccurrence is the same-name occurrence. FieldNumber is one-based, or zero for a segment finding. Segment position zero denotes a message-level PID-3 identity finding.
Entries.Returns: Findings snapshot and CSV projection; Path and Description use only fixed text, enum vocabulary and numeric coordinates.
Entries.Limitations: At most 1,000 occurrence rows per run. Summary.OmittedFindings discloses further occurrences; summary counts remain exact. Findings and counter types can overlap. Workspace maps processed ordinals to captured logical positions, including Current message scope. These are supported-policy findings, not a comprehensive PHI detector. No raw patient values, dates, filenames or identity crosswalks.
Entries.Keywords: DeidentificationFinding findings path reason review CSV privacy retained
